study: AI hold-check (shadow): asked once at ~11:00 ET whether a day-hold-eligible name should be held to 15:54 or exited now, does the AI's EXIT call pick names whose remaining return is worse than the names it says to HOLD, by more than a price-only rule with the same number of exits?
registered_at: 2026-10-09 (Friday, RTH; before any logger, prompt run or outcome exists)
origin: Operator 10/9: 'can we use AI on our names that we have opened to see if our entries make sense to hold'. Desk trades last 3-10 min, too short for an AI call; the day-hold names are held for hours. The AI can read news and sentiment, which no desk indicator sees.
prior: LOW. Every exit rule tested (42 shapes) moved the win rate, never the mean (memory exits-cannot-move-the-mean). Fresh news in the last 60 min made entries worse (daily-context study, 9/23): news gets chased then fades. No AI-judgment test on this desk has passed. The one reason to try: news is genuinely new information to the desk.
shadow_only: Nothing the AI says is acted on. The day-hold prereg (docs/studies/day_hold_prereg.json), its picks, exits and 40-session read are unchanged, and no live desk setting changes. The logger must not place, modify or cancel any order.

population.qualify_time: at ~10:46 ET each session, from DELAYED SIP 1-min bars stamped 09:30-10:29 (complete and free by then), using day_hold.py load_candidates / morning / qualifies / rank_key exactly as the nightly forward run (no IEX qualification).
population.checked: up to 30 names a session: first every name that qualifies under the day-hold rule (by rank_key), then names drawn at random (seed sha256('aihold|' + day)) from the day's ELIGIBLE pool (day-hold candidates with P >= $10 and 09:30-10:29 dollar volume >= $5M, the C1 pool of day_hold_prereg.json) until 30. Pilot counts (14 days): ~2 qualifiers and ~40 eligible a day.
population.scored: a name-day is SCORED when its own SIP bars for the day are complete (day_hold's day-level >5%-missing abort does NOT apply here) and the main day-hold exit rule (loss limit entry x 0.97 from the 10:30 open, red knife, 15:54) has not exited it before the answer bar. These filters apply identically to HOLD and EXIT answers and do not depend on the answer. Others are logged and counted.

checks: ONE check per name per session, starting 11:00 ET; calls may run up to 4 at a time; the answer timestamp is logged. Calls whose answer arrives more than 180 s after the call started are counted and NOT scored (latency cap).

model_and_prompt.model: the AGY slot as configured in bot_config.json on the day (agy CLI, gemini-3.1-pro-high on 10/9), web search allowed; recorded per call. A change of model mid-study is logged; the read reports by model but the verdict pools them.
model_and_prompt.prompt: frozen in tools/studies/ai_hold_check.py as PROMPT_V1 before the first session, sha256 logged with every call. Inputs given: symbol, company name, 10:30 entry price, current price, % from entry, today's high/low/open, prior close, time ET, and the instruction to answer HOLD (keep to 15:54) or EXIT (sell now) with a confidence 1-5 and one sentence citing any news. No P&L history, no other names' outcomes, no desk opinions.
model_and_prompt.parse: normalize: strip markdown (*, _, #, `), whitespace and case; the first token must be HOLD or EXIT; anything else = unparseable (counted, not scored).
model_and_prompt.search: SUPERSEDED by amended_2: news is supplied from the Alpaca news feed; no web access is used.

outcome: per scored name-day: remaining = (the main day-hold rule's exit price, scanning SIP bars from the first bar that STARTS after the answer timestamp: loss limit, red knife or the 15:54 close, per day_hold.simulate) / (the open of that first post-answer bar) - 1, in bp. Exiting at the answer and holding to the rule's exit are each one sale, so no cost difference is charged.

statistic.ai: per session: mean remaining of HOLD name-days minus mean remaining of EXIT name-days (a session needs >= 1 of each; sessions without are counted and excluded).
statistic.twin_pct: price-only twin: in the same session, among the same scored name-days, label EXIT the same number of names as the AI did, chosen as the worst % from the 10:30 entry at the answer bar; the rest HOLD; same statistic. Ties broken by symbol, ascending.
statistic.twin_range: second twin: the same number chosen by lowest position in the day's range at the answer bar. Ties broken by symbol, ascending.
statistic.primary: per session: AI statistic minus twin_pct statistic; mean over sessions, t across sessions.
statistic.policy: INFORMATION ONLY: day-hold top-3 picks under the main rule vs the same picks exited at the AI's EXIT, compared with a random-EXIT control (the same number of exits drawn among the picks, 200 seeded draws).

read: ONE read, at the first close with >= 30 scored sessions (a scored session has at least one scored HOLD and one scored EXIT name-day) AND >= 150 scored EXIT and >= 150 scored HOLD name-days (distinct name-days). If not reached by 45 sessions: UNDERPOWERED = FAIL. Before the read only counts (sessions, calls, parse failures, latency drops, EXIT/HOLD split, search use) may be looked at, never outcomes.
pass: AI minus twin_pct >= +25 bp per session with t >= 2.0, positive in both halves (alternate sessions), still >= +25 bp with t >= 2.0 after dropping the best session; AND AI minus twin_range > 0. A pass earns a skeptic review, then a pre-registered paper switch-on of AI exits for day-hold names only. Never live money first.
fail: anything else is FAIL; the AI hold-check is then closed for day-hold names.
data_integrity: failed or unparseable calls are dropped and counted; a session is excluded only for a logger outage covering the 11:00 check or a rate-limit stop before 15 calls (counted); > 25% of sessions excluded aborts as FAILED-DATA. Every call is logged raw (prompt hash, inputs, output, start/answer timestamps, latency, model, tool use) to ai_reports/ai_hold_check/<day>.jsonl before any outcome exists.
cost_and_load: subscription slots only (no per-call billing); hard cap 30 calls a session, at most 4 concurrent; the logger stops for the day on the FIRST rate-limit or quota error from agy, and logs the desk's own agy errors per session so any effect on desk research (and so on day_hold's 'agy' source family) is visible; usage recorded under its own phase ('ai_hold_check'); runs at nice 10; one delayed-SIP bars request at 10:46 plus one daily-bars request; started by the LaunchAgent or a local Terminal on the mini, never over ssh (agy's Keychain session is unreadable from ssh); deployed after a close.
caveats: LLM answers are not reproducible; the raw log is the record
the AI may lean HOLD on up names; HOLD minus EXIT within a session controls the day's market move but not name-level momentum
the eligible names are not all day-hold picks; the verdict is about the AI's hold judgment on this pool, applied to picks only via the policy line
web search with agy may need read_url permission; the smoke test gates the start
UNDERPOWERED is a likely ending: ~20 scored names a session need the AI to say EXIT ~17-25% of the time to reach 150 EXIT name-days in 30-45 sessions; that rate is unknown
script: tools/studies/ai_hold_check.py (logger + nightly scorer), written after this file is committed; it may not change anything above
amended: 2026-10-09, before any logger, prompt or outcome, per the result-skeptic FIX FIRST: SIP qualification at 10:46 (IEX cannot meet $5M); outcome from the first bar after the answer + 180 s latency cap; price-only twins (pct-from-entry primary, range second) as the bar; one check per name-day at 11:00; population widened to qualifiers + seeded eligible names up to 30 (pilot: ~2 qualifiers, ~40 eligible a day); per-name bar completeness, not day_hold's day abort; 150/150 distinct name-days; policy line vs random-EXIT control, information only; parse normalization; failed calls dropped, sessions excluded only for outages; search logging + smoke test gate; quota stop, desk agy error logging, own usage phase, LaunchAgent/Terminal only. Round 2 (skeptic OK): scored-session definition, twin tie-break by symbol, smoke test also logs concurrent latency and the share already exited by 11:00, UNDERPOWERED risk stated.
amended_2: 2026-10-09 ~16:20 ET, BEFORE the study started (no session logged): the smoke test FAILED its gate. The AI answered a search question in 1 turn with no tool use and gave an NVIDIA '$1 billion quantum/healthcare/energy' headline that a web search could not find (likely invented). Web access is not enabled on the mini, and enabling it globally would change the desk's research calls (and so day_hold's 'AI' source family) mid-test. CHANGE: the logger supplies the news itself. Before each call it fetches the name's headlines from Alpaca's news feed (NewsClient, free with the existing data keys; Benzinga), created from the prior session's 16:00 ET close up to the call's start time (never later), newest first, at most 10, each as 'HH:MM ET | source | headline' plus the first 200 characters of its summary. The prompt becomes PROMPT_V2 (frozen, sha256 logged): the same inputs and answer format, plus the headline block, and the instruction to judge only from the data and headlines given, not to search or rely on memory, and to say 'no news' when the block is empty. Every call logs the headline ids and timestamps it was given. The news-fetch call is one batched request per check (all names), so load is unchanged. NEW SMOKE GATE (replaces the search gate): (a) the news fetch returns >= 1 headline for at least half of 5 liquid names (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, TSLA) over the prior 24 h; (b) on a call given headlines, the answer's reason cites one of the given headlines (substring of >= 5 consecutive words or the headline's distinctive entity), checked by hand on the smoke output and logged; (c) on a call given an EMPTY block, the reason says no news. If the gate fails, the study does not start. Information: the share of calls with >= 1 headline, and the HOLD/EXIT result split by 'had news' vs 'no news' (not a verdict). Nothing else changes: population, timing, twins, statistic, pass bar, read. Skeptic FIX FIRST on this amendment, applied before start: (1) news is fetched LIVE only, once per check, the window ending at the FETCH time (logged); a missed session is never backfilled; every call logs each given headline's id, created_at, updated_at, headline and summary exactly as given. (2) Each headline line is dated 'MM-DD HH:MM ET'; information split: names with a headline created after 10:30 vs only older. (3) New twin 'twin_news': in each session label EXIT the same number of names as the AI, drawn first from had-news names (worst % from entry first), then from no-news names (worst first; ties by symbol). PASS additionally requires AI minus twin_news > 0 (as twin_range). The had-news/no-news split stays information. (4) Smoke gate made mechanical: (b) passes only if the normalized reason shares >= 5 consecutive words with a given headline or summary, or contains a headline token (>= 4 letters) that is not the symbol, the company name or a stopword; the match is logged. (c) is run on NVDA with an EMPTY block and must match /no news/i. Both checks run on every session call as counts (empty block but cites news; given headlines but cites none) reported by status. (5) News is paged until exhausted (no silent truncation), then capped at 10 per name; each name's raw count is logged; a fetch error is recorded as an error, never as 'no news' (that session's calls are excluded from the had-news split, counted). (6) num_turns > 1 per call is logged as a contamination count.
